inlines.v: JOURNEY, noun jur'ny. [Latin diurnus, dies.] 1. The travel of a day. 2. Travel by land to any distance and for any time, indefinitely; as a journey from London to Paris, or to Rome; a journey to visit a brother; a week's journey; we made two journeys to Philadelphia. 3. Passage form one place to another; as a long journey from the upper regions. 4. It may sometimes include a passing by water. JOURNEY, verb intransitive jur'ny. To travel form place to place; to pass from home to a distance. Abram journeyed, going on still towards the south. Genesis 12:9.
